title: “Every Woman in the World” by Air Supply
text: "Every Woman in the World" is a song by British/Australian soft rock duo Air Supply. The song was written by Dominic Bugatti and Frank Musker.
listen: Every Woman in the World Air Supply

title: “The One That You Love”
text: "The One That You Love" is a song by British-Australian soft rock duo Air Supply, released as a single from their sixth studio album of the same name. It was written by member Graham Russell.

title: “Guilty” by Barbra Streisand & Barry Gibb
text: "Guilty" is a vocal duet between Barbra Streisand and Barry Gibb. The song was written by all three Bee Gees: Barry, Robin & Maurice Gibb.
wiki: Guilty (Barbra Streisand and Barry Gibb song)

title: “The Best of Times” by Styx
text: "The Best of Times" is a song by American rock band Styx, released as the first single from their tenth album Paradise Theatre. It reached No.

title: “Elvira” by The Oak Ridge Boys
text: "Elvira" is a song written and originally recorded by Dallas Frazier. Though a minor hit for Frazier at the time of release, the song became a major pop and country hit for the Oak Ridge Boys in 1981.

title: “Take It on the Run” by REO Speedwagon
text: "Take It on the Run" is a song by American rock band REO Speedwagon off the band's ninth studio album Hi Infidelity. The song was written by lead guitarist Gary Richrath.
listen: Take It on the Run REO Speedwagon

title: “(There's) No Gettin' Over Me” by Ronnie Milsap
text: " No Gettin' Over Me" is a song written by Walt Aldridge and Tom Brasfield, and recorded by American country music singer Ronnie Milsap. It was released in June 1981 as the first single from the album There's No Gettin' Over Me.
listen: (There's) No Gettin' Over Me Ronnie Milsap

title: “Living Inside Myself” by Gino Vannelli
text: "Living Inside Myself" is a song written and performed by Canadian singer-songwriter Gino Vannelli. It appears on his seventh album, Nightwalker.

title: “Woman in Love” by Barbra Streisand
text: "Woman in Love" is a song performed by Barbra Streisand and taken from her 1980 album Guilty. The song was written by Barry and Robin Gibb of the Bee Gees, who received the 1980 Ivor Novello award for Best Song Musically and Lyrically.

title: “The Boy from New York City” by The Manhattan Transfer
text: "The Boy from New York City" is a song originally recorded by the American soul group The Ad Libs, released in 1964 as their first single. Produced by Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller, the song peaked at No.
wiki: The Boy from New York City
listen: The Boy from New York City The Manhattan Transfer

title: “Urgent” by Foreigner
text: "Urgent" is a song by the British-American rock band Foreigner, and the first single from their album 4 in 1981.

title: “Passion” by Rod Stewart
text: "Passion" is a song by Rod Stewart that first appeared in 1980 on his album Foolish Behaviour. It was the lead single and biggest hit from the album, reaching number five on the US Billboard Hot 100, number two in Canada, and a sizeable hit across Europe.

title: “Lady (You Bring Me Up)” by Commodores
text: "Lady" is a 1981 hit single by the Commodores. In the United States, it peaked at No.

title: “Crying” by Don McLean
text: "Crying" is a song written by the American singer, songwriter, and guitarist Roy Orbison and Joe Melson for Orbison's third album Crying. Released in 1961, it was a number-two hit in the United States for Orbison and was covered in 1978 by Don McLean, whose version reached number one in the United Kingdom in 1980.

title: “Hearts” by Marty Balin
text: "Hearts" is a song written by Jesse Barish and performed by Marty Balin in 1981, included on his debut solo album Balin. It was Balin's third single in nineteen years and the biggest hit of his solo career.

title: “It's My Turn” by Diana Ross
text: "It's My Turn" is a song sung by American singer Diana Ross as the theme to the film It's My Turn. With lyrics written by Carole Bayer Sager, and Michael Masser composing and producing, the song was released on September 29, 1980 by Motown as the lead single from the film's soundtrack of the same name as the song and its parent movie.

title: “You Make My Dreams” by Daryl Hall & John Oates
text: "You Make My Dreams" is a song by American duo Daryl Hall & John Oates, taken from their ninth studio album, Voices. The song reached number five on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in 1981.
listen: You Make My Dreams Daryl Hall & John Oates

title: “I Don't Need You” by Kenny Rogers
text: "I Don't Need You" is a song written by Rick Christian, and was first recorded and released as a single in 1978 on Mercury Records, by Rick Christian himself at Shoe Productions, a recording studio/production company in Memphis, Tennessee, but it failed to chart.
listen: I Don't Need You Kenny Rogers

title: “How 'Bout Us” by Champaign
text: "How 'Bout Us" is the most successful single released by R&B music group Champaign. Composed by band keyboardist Dana Walden and originally released on the band's debut album How 'Bout Us, the title track peaked at number 12 on the Billboard Hot 100.

title: “Hit Me with Your Best Shot” by Pat Benatar
text: "Hit Me with Your Best Shot" is a song recorded by American rock singer Pat Benatar and written by Eddie Schwartz. In 1980, it was released as the second single from her second album Crimes of Passion, which became her biggest-selling album.
wiki: Hit Me with Your Best Shot
listen: Hit Me with Your Best Shot Pat Benatar

title: “The Breakup Song (They Don't Write 'Em)” by The Greg Kihn Band
text: "The Breakup Song" is a song written by Greg Kihn and Steve Wright and recorded by the American rock band the Greg Kihn Band. It is the first single from the band's sixth studio album, RocKihnRoll (1981).
listen: The Breakup Song (They Don't Write 'Em) The Greg Kihn Band

title: “Time” by The Alan Parsons Project
text: "Time" is a song released in 1981 as a single by the Alan Parsons Project. It was from their 1980 album The Turn of a Friendly Card.

title: “Hungry Heart” by Bruce Springsteen
text: "Hungry Heart" is a rock song written and performed by the American singer-songwriter Bruce Springsteen on his fifth album, The River. It was released as the album's lead single in 1980 and became Springsteen's first top-five hit on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number five.

title: “Sweetheart” by Franke and the Knockouts
text: "Sweetheart" is the debut single by Franke and the Knockouts. It is their greatest hit, reaching the U.S. top 10 during the spring of 1981.

title: “Somebody's Knockin'” by Terri Gibbs
text: "Somebody's Knockin'" is a song recorded by American country music singer Terri Gibbs. It was released in October 1980 as her debut single and title track from her album Somebody's Knockin'.

title: “More Than I Can Say” by Leo Sayer
text: "More Than I Can Say" is a song written by Sonny Curtis and Jerry Allison, both former members of Buddy Holly's band the Crickets. They recorded it in 1959 soon after Holly's death and released it in 1960.
listen: More Than I Can Say Leo Sayer

title: “Together” by Tierra
text: "Together" is a 1967 song originally recorded and performed by The Intruders. The song reached number 48 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 and spent nine weeks on the chart.

title: “Too Much Time on My Hands” by Styx
text: "Too Much Time on My Hands" is a song by American rock band Styx, released as the second single from their tenth album Paradise Theatre. It was written and sung by Tommy Shaw, who also plays the lead guitar solo during the break in the song.
wiki: Too Much Time on My Hands
listen: Too Much Time on My Hands Styx

title: “What Are We Doin' in Love” by Dottie West & Kenny Rogers
text: "What Are We Doin' in Love" is a song written by Randy Goodrum and recorded by American country music artist Dottie West. Although not credited on the single release, the song also features American country and pop recording artist Kenny Rogers.
wiki: What Are We Doin' in Love
listen: What Are We Doin' in Love Dottie West & Kenny Rogers

title: “Who's Crying Now” by Journey
text: "Who's Crying Now" is a song by the American rock band Journey. It was written by Jonathan Cain and Steve Perry.

title: A powerful Ms 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits Athens, killing 22 people, injuring 400 people and destroying several buildings and 4,000 houses, mostly in Corinth and the nearby towns of Loutraki, Kiato and Xylokastro.
text: Kiato is a town in the northern part of Corinthia in the Peloponnese, Greece. It is the seat of the municipality of Sikyona.

title: 1981 Irish hunger strike: Bobby Sands, a Provisional Irish Republican Army member, begins a hunger strike for political status at HM Prison Maze (Long Kesh) in Northern Ireland, dying on May 5, the first of 7 IRA and 3 INLA hunger strikers…
text: A five-year protest during the Troubles by Irish republican prisoners in Northern Ireland culminated in a hunger strike in 1981. The protest began as the blanket protest in 1976 when the British government withdrew Special Category Status for convicted paramilitary prisoners.

title: Chilean military dictator Augusto Pinochet is sworn in as President of Chile for another 8-year term.
text: Augusto José Ramón Pinochet Ugarte was a Chilean army officer and military dictator who ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990. He led the Chilean Army in the overthrow of President Salvador Allende in 1973 and established a military junta.

title: In Italy, the Propaganda Due Masonic lodge is discovered.
text: A Masonic lodge is the basic organisational unit of Freemasonry. It is also a commonly used term for a building where Freemasons meet and hold their meetings.

title: Two or three workers are killed and four are injured during a ground test of Space Shuttle Columbia at Kennedy Space Center in the United States.
text: Space Shuttle Columbia was a Space Shuttle orbiter manufactured by Rockwell International and operated by NASA. Named after the first American ship to circumnavigate the globe, and the female personification of the United States, Columbia was the first of five Space Shuttle orbiters to fly in space, debuting the Space Shuttle launch vehicle on its maiden flight on April 12, 1981 and becoming the first spacecraft t…

title: The first London Marathon starts, with 7,500 runners.
text: The London Marathon is an annual marathon held in London, England. Founded by athletes Chris Brasher and John Disley in 1981, it is typically held in April, although it moved to October for 2020, 2021, and 2022 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Attempted assassination of Ronald Reagan: U.S. President Ronald Reagan is shot in the chest outside a Washington, D.C., hotel by John Hinckley Jr.; two police officers and Press Secretary James Brady are also wounded.
text: On March 30, 1981, Ronald Reagan, the president of the United States, was shot and wounded by John Hinckley Jr. outside of the Washington Hilton in Washington, D.C., as Reagan was returning to his limousine after a speaking engagement at the hotel.

title: UK pop group Bucks Fizz's song "Making Your Mind Up" wins the 1981 Eurovision Song Contest in Dublin, Ireland.
text: Bucks Fizz are an English pop group that achieved success in the 1980s, most notably for winning the Eurovision Song Contest 1981 with the song "Making Your Mind Up". The group was formed in January 1981 specifically for the contest and comprised four vocalists: Bobby G, Cheryl Baker, Mike Nolan and Jay Aston.

title: The Space Shuttle program: Space Shuttle Columbia, with NASA astronauts John Young and Robert Crippen, launches on the STS-1 mission, returning to Earth on April 14. It is the first time a crewed reusable spacecraft has returned from orbit.
text: The Space Shuttle is a retired, partially reusable low Earth orbital spacecraft system that went to the ISS and performed other orbital missions. Operated from 1981 to 2011 by the U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration as part of the Space Shuttle program.

title: The first Coca-Cola bottling plant in China is opened.
text: Coca-Cola, or Coke, is a cola soft drink manufactured by the Coca-Cola Company. In 2013, Coke products were sold in over 200 countries and territories worldwide, with consumers drinking more than 1.8 billion company beverage servings each day.

title: A Minor League Baseball game between the Rochester Red Wings and the Pawtucket Red Sox at McCoy Stadium in Pawtucket, Rhode Island, becomes the longest professional baseball game in history: 8 hours and 25 minutes/33 innings (the 33rd…
text: The Pawtucket Red Sox, known colloquially as the PawSox, were a professional minor league baseball club based in Pawtucket, Rhode Island. From 1973 to 2020, the team was a member of the International League and served as the Triple-A affiliate of the Boston Red Sox.

title: French presidential election: A first-round runoff results between Valéry Giscard d'Estaing and François Mitterrand.
text: Valéry René Marie Georges Giscard d'Estaing, also known as simply Giscard or VGE, was President of France from 1974 to 1981. After serving as Minister of Finance under prime ministers Jacques Chaban-Delmas and Pierre Messmer, Giscard d'Estaing won the presidential election of 1974 with 50.8% of the vote against François Mitterrand of the Socialist Party.

title: Daniel K. Ludwig abandons the Jari project in the Amazon basin.
text: The Jari project was an attempt to create a tropical tree farm in Brazil for producing pulp for paper.

title: Aer Lingus flight 164 is hijacked just before landing at London Heathrow airport. The flight continues on to France before the hijacker who reportedly demanded for the releasing of the third secret of Fatima, is subdued.
text: Aer Lingus Flight 164 was a scheduled Boeing 737-200 passenger flight that was hijacked on 2 May 1981, on route from Dublin in Ireland to London in England.

title: A jury of architects and sculptors unanimously selects Maya Lin's design for the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., from among 1,421 other entries.
text: Maya Ying Lin is an American architect, designer, and sculptor. Born in Athens, Ohio, to Chinese immigrants, she attended Yale University to study architecture.

title: The Jamaican reggae singer Bob Marley dies at age 36 from cancer.
text: Robert Nesta Marley was a Jamaican reggae singer, songwriter, and guitarist. Considered one of the pioneers of the genre, he was renowned for his distinctive vocal and songwriting style.

title: Pope John Paul II assassination attempt: Pope John Paul II is shot by Mehmet Ali Ağca, a Turkish gunman, as he enters St. Peter's Square in Vatican City to address a general audience. The Pope recovers.
text: On 13 May 1981, in St. Peter's Square in Vatican City, Pope John Paul II was shot and wounded by Mehmet Ali Ağca while he was entering the square.
wiki: Attempted assassination of Pope John Paul II

title: A prison officer, 31-year-old Donna Payant, disappears at Green Haven Correctional Facility in New York. She is later found to have been murdered by convicted serial killer Lemuel Smith. It is the first time a female prison officer has…
text: Lemuel Warren Smith is an American convicted serial killer who was the first convict to kill an on-duty female corrections officer. Smith was already in prison for the murders of at least five people when he murdered prison guard Donna Payant at Green Haven Correctional Facility in 1981.

title: François Mitterrand becomes the first socialist President of the French Fifth Republic.
text: François Marie Adrien Maurice Mitterrand was President of France from 1981 to 1995. He was the first left-wing politician to assume the presidency under the Fifth Republic, successfully remaining in office longer than any other republican head of state in French history.

title: Serial killer Peter Sutcliffe is found guilty and sentenced to life imprisonment on 13 counts of murder and 7 of attempted murder in England.
text: Peter William Sutcliffe, also known as Peter Coonan, was an English serial killer who was convicted of murdering thirteen women and girls, and attempting to murder seven others between 1975 and 1980. Press reports dubbed him the "Yorkshire Ripper", an allusion to the Victorian serial killer Jack the Ripper.

title: In Riyadh, the Gulf Cooperation Council is created among Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
text: The Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf, also known as the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC; Arabic: مجلس التعاون الخليجي), is a regional, intergovernmental, political, economic union, and military alliance comprising Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. The council's main headquarters is located in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia.

title: The Italian Forlani government resigns over its links to the fascist Masonic cell Propaganda Due.
text: The Forlani Cabinet, led by Arnaldo Forlani, was the 38th cabinet of the Italian Republic. The government was composed of the DC, PSI, PSDI and PRI, with the abstention of the PLI. Since in the Italian Senate the abstention is valid as a contrary vote, the two senators of the PLI did not take part in the vote of confidence to the government.
